drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Counsel,

Attached is our revised draft. We have tightened the closing mechanics by tying Closing to satisfaction or waiver of the stated conditions, added a Closing bring-down for Seller’s representations, removed the knowledge qualifier from the financial-statement representation, and expanded the indemnity provision to specify scope, limitations, and procedures in the agreement text.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur on the third (3rd) Business Day after the satisfaction or written waiver of the conditions to Closing set forth in this Agreement, or on such other date as the Parties may agree in writing. At Closing, each Party shall deliver the customary closing documents reasonably required to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including evidence of authority, transfer instruments, and any required certificates or consents.
edits.name: Revise closing mechanics

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. The Seller represents that the financial statements provided to Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented, in accordance with the accounting principles consistently applied in their preparation. The Seller further represents that each representation and warranty of the Seller in this Agreement shall be true and correct in all material respects as of the Closing, except for representations and warranties that expressly relate to an earlier date, which shall be true and correct in all material respects as of such earlier date.
edits.name: Revise financial statement representation and add bring-down

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. From and after Closing, the Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer and its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, members, managers, employees, agents, successors, and assigns, from and against any and all losses, liabilities, damages, deficiencies, claims, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from: (a) any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty made by the Seller in this Agreement; (b) any breach or non-performance of any covenant or agreement of the Seller in this Agreement; and (c) any liabilities of the Company arising from facts, events, or circumstances occurring or existing prior to Closing, except to the extent expressly assumed by Buyer or expressly reflected in the final closing statement. Buyer shall provide Seller with reasonably prompt written notice of any claim for indemnification, provided that failure to provide prompt notice shall relieve Seller only to the extent Seller is materially prejudiced thereby. Seller shall have the right to participate in the defense of any third-party claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to Buyer, and Buyer shall not settle any such claim in a manner imposing non-monetary obligations on Seller without Seller’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Indemnification for breaches of representations and warranties shall be subject to a deductible equal to one percent (1%) of the Purchase Price and an aggregate cap equal to ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price, except that claims arising from fraud, willful misconduct, intentional misrepresentation, or breaches of fundamental representations shall not be subject to such deductible or cap. Claims for breaches of representations and warranties must be asserted within eighteen (18) months after Closing, except that fundamental representations shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations.
edits.name: Expand indemnity scope, limitations, and procedures
